heroHeadline: Trump Pauses 'Project Freedom,' Cites 'Great Progress' in US-Iran Talks — Framework Memo to End War and Reopen Strait of Hormuz Under Development
heroSubtitle: On May 6, 2026, President Trump announced a pause to 'Project Freedom' — the Strait of Hormuz military escort operation launched just two days earlier — citing 'great progress' in peace talks with Iran. CNN reported the US and Iran are 'moving toward a memo aimed at ending the war,' which would declare an end to the conflict and trigger a 30-day transition period addressing the Strait re-opening, naval blockade lift, asset unfreezing, and nuclear talks timeline. Al Jazeera framed the development as a potential US concession on the core sequencing dispute: Iran has demanded Hormuz be resolved before nuclear negotiations, and Tehran's Foreign Ministry is reviewing the US reply to its latest proposal. A day earlier, on May 5, an Iranian official publicly confirmed the Hormuz-first sequencing while Trump signaled 'very positive discussions' were underway — a notable shift from the confrontational posture of May 3–4. The Lebanon ceasefire monitoring mechanism remains strained heading toward its ~May 14 expiry, with IDF operations continuing in south Lebanon, though that track is linked to any US-Iran framework. Ethiopia called for an immediate humanitarian truce in Sudan, and Thailand's foreign minister sought ASEAN engagement on Myanmar — demonstrating the breadth of simultaneous peace process activity globally. The US-Iran breakthrough is the most consequential positive diplomatic development in the tracker since the conflict began, though a framework memo remains unsigned and implementation uncertain.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
